business_process: Reservoir and spillway gate operations (including flood passage)
description: Set gate openings at 41 gated dams to follow reservoir operating plans and license limits; pass floods; coordinate releases along each river system
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Life safety: loss of gate control during a flood could overtop a dam, and a wrong opening sends a surge toward downstream communities (DEV-04 alone has a city of about 38,000 in its inundation zone). If the HOC is lost, plants fall back to local gate panels, which needs operators dispatched to unattended dams; the MTD is the time to staff the 23 Group 1 and 2 dams safely during high flow. RPO covers gate position and reservoir history in the historian
manual_workaround: Failover to HOC-B; operators dispatched to local gate panels with radio contact (call-out plan by river system); standby-generator or hand-crank operation; reservoir read from staff gauges
dependent_third_parties: Telecom carriers (DEP-04, DEP-05); fleet SCADA vendor; standby generator fuel suppliers
dependent_people_or_facilities: HOC operators; plant on-call crews (minimum 2 per gated Group 1 or 2 dam during floods); HOC-A; HOC-B
quantified_impact_basis: Safety dominates. Cost is overtime and dispatch of about 180 staff to local panels (about $0.25 million per day) plus forced spill and lost flexibility at the largest reservoirs (about $0.2 million per day)
acquired_asset_dependency: PD-04 and PD-06 gates run locally today; no HOC fallback until integration (DEP-18, DEP-19)
single_points_of_failure: HOC fleet SCADA (two sites, failover not meeting RTO); single carrier at 19 plants

business_process: Dam safety monitoring and EAP early warning
description: Read about 3,900 instruments at 52 dams against trigger points; detect developing failure modes; activate 126 sirens at 18 dams and make EAP notifications
process_owner: Vice President, Dam Safety (Chief Dam Safety Engineer)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Life safety and 18 CFR 12.10 (unusual instrumentation readings are reportable conditions, 12.3(b)(4)(viii)). Data loggers buffer 30 days of readings, so data loss is limited, but trend review and alerting stop; manual readings must start within 4 hours at High hazard dams
manual_workaround: Manual instrument readings every 4 hours by dam safety technicians at High hazard dams (daily at others); local siren activation at each siren pole; EAP phone trees from printed binders
dependent_third_parties: Cellular carriers for 87 gauges (DEP-21); siren maintenance contractor; county emergency management agencies (DEP-17)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Dam safety technicians (about 140); regional dam safety engineers; Chief Dam Safety Engineer
quantified_impact_basis: Technician overtime and travel for manual readings at 52 dams; safety impact dominates
acquired_asset_dependency: PD dams use the prior owner's dataloggers; readings reach the DSMS only by daily file upload
single_points_of_failure: Cellular modems for remote gauges (single carrier per gauge)

description: Start, load, and stop 151 units to schedules and Balancing Authority dispatch; automatic generation control; protect units
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $10.0 million of generation revenue per calendar day. Units can run locally at reduced flexibility, but regulation service and automatic generation control stop and imbalance charges start. Water not used for generation passes through spillways, which BP-01 must manage
manual_workaround: Failover to HOC-B; local unit control at staffed plants; voice dispatch from the Balancing Authorities; block-loading to the day-ahead schedule
dependent_third_parties: Balancing Authorities A and B (DEP-08, DEP-09); fleet SCADA vendor (DEP-07); governor and excitation OEM (DEP-06)
dependent_people_or_facilities: HOC operators; plant operators and mechanics; HOC-A; HOC-B
quantified_impact_basis: About 30% of daily generation value lost or deferred (reduced flexibility, lost regulation and reserve payments, imbalance charges) at $10.0 million per day
acquired_asset_dependency: PD plants are dispatched by phone from the scheduling desk
single_points_of_failure: Governor and excitation OEM remote service for 60% of units

description: Pump and generate at DEV-01 (1,320 MW) and DEV-03 (780 MW) to capacity and energy schedules; manage upper and lower reservoirs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Capacity obligations and arbitrage value; upper reservoirs at DEV-01 and DEV-03 are Group 1 dams, so overfilling in pumping mode is a safety condition. Pumping stops automatically on loss of control; generation can run locally
manual_workaround: Stop pumping; local generation only; upper reservoir levels monitored by on-site staff
dependent_third_parties: Balancing Authority A (DEP-08); fleet SCADA vendor (DEP-07)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Pumped storage operators at DEV-01 and DEV-03
quantified_impact_basis: Capacity non-performance charges and lost arbitrage for 2,100 MW of pumped storage

description: Keep 6 Blackstart Resources and regulation and reserve capability available under the Balancing Authority agreements and the Transmission Operators' restoration plans
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contract and reliability obligations: the Transmission Operators rely on the 6 Blackstart Resources to restore the grid after a blackout. Loss of HOC control does not stop blackstart units, which can start locally, but readiness reporting and remote start do
manual_workaround: Local blackstart procedures at each Blackstart Resource with on-call crews; voice coordination with the Transmission Operator
dependent_third_parties: Transmission Operators and Balancing Authorities (DEP-08, DEP-09)
quantified_impact_basis: Lost ancillary service payments and contract penalties

business_process: Real-time data exchange with Balancing Authorities and Transmission Operators
description: ICCP links from HOC-A and HOC-B to the two Balancing Authorities and Transmission Operators: unit status, MW, dispatch instructions (CIP-012-2 scope)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Reliability coordination: without real-time data the Balancing Authorities fall back to voice and may restrict the fleet. Loss of data exchange between Control Centers is a CIP-012-2 availability scenario
manual_workaround: Voice communication on recorded lines; manual hourly MW reports; second ICCP path through HOC-B
dependent_third_parties: Balancing Authorities A and B; telecom carriers (DEP-04, DEP-05)
quantified_impact_basis: Restrictions and imbalance exposure while on voice coordination
single_points_of_failure: HOC-B ICCP uses one carrier entrance

description: Day-ahead and real-time schedules, bilateral trades, ancillary service bids, and offtaker settlements (SYS-11)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash and contracts: a missed day-ahead submission leaves the fleet unscheduled for the next day. Settlement can be rebuilt from meter data, so the RPO is 1 hour for schedules
manual_workaround: Schedules submitted through the Balancing Authority portals by the scheduling desk using printed templates; phone confirmations with offtakers
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A (DEP-11); scheduling platform vendor (DEP-24); offtakers (DEP-10)
quantified_impact_basis: Imbalance and missed day-ahead positions at about 24% of daily generation value
single_points_of_failure: Scheduling platform vendor (single product, no alternate)

business_process: Physical security monitoring and access control
description: PACS at the HOCs (CIP-006 scope), cameras and intrusion detection at Group 1 and 2 dams, security dispatch
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: CIP-006-6 requires monitoring of Physical Security Perimeters and alerts within 15 minutes; Security Plans for Group 1 and 2 dams require threat-level responses; FERC expects incident reports usually within one working day
manual_workaround: Posted security officers at HOC entrances; extra patrols at Group 1 and 2 dams; manual visitor logs
dependent_third_parties: Security systems integrator; security officer contractor at 6 dams; local law enforcement
dependent_people_or_facilities: Security officers; security dispatch at HOC-A
acquired_asset_dependency: PD-04 and PD-06 cameras are on the prior owner's system, not monitored by security dispatch

description: Local operation of 9 developments (412 MW, 11 dams) with after-hours remote access, until integration onto the HOC
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: PD-04 and PD-06 are Security Group 2 dams with gated spillways and downstream populations; PD-02, PD-04, and PD-06 are BES plants. Daytime staff can run gates and units locally; nights depend on the legacy VPN for remote monitoring
manual_workaround: Local operators on site; night shift staffing at PD-04 and PD-06 during high flows; phone dispatch
dependent_third_parties: Piedmont SCADA integrator (DEP-18); legacy VPN concentrator (DEP-19); governor OEM (DEP-06)
dependent_people_or_facilities: PD plant operators (46); PD plant managers
quantified_impact_basis: 412 MW of generation at about $1,165 per MW-day
acquired_asset_dependency: All nine developments (this process exists only because of the acquisition)
single_points_of_failure: One integrator and one VPN concentrator for all 9 plants; never restore-tested

business_process: SL-1 contract remote operations for client plants
description: The Contract Operations Center monitors and, on owner instruction, operates 27 non-BES plants of 11 clients through client-owned VPN endpoints
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Client commitments (contract availability of 99.9% for monitoring) and the clients' own dam safety: several client plants have gated spillways. Clients must staff their plants if the COC is down
manual_workaround: Clients staff their plants locally under the contract fallback clause; COC operators call client on-call staff
dependent_third_parties: Client VPN endpoints (DEP-20); Cloud provider B (portal, DEP-12)
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits and client staffing costs under 11 contracts; reputational effect on the SOC 2 report (P09)
single_points_of_failure: COC is a single site; the backup position at HOC-B is untested for SL-1

description: The DSMS collects instrument data and sends alerts for 138 client dams of 46 clients and the company's own 52 instrumented dams; includes AI-001
process_owner: Vice President, Dam Safety Monitoring Services
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Clients rely on DSMS alerts as part of their surveillance programs; a missed alert could delay response to a developing failure mode. Readings arrive every 15 minutes, so the RPO is one reading interval
manual_workaround: Clients take manual readings under their own surveillance plans; DSMS analysts phone High hazard clients
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider B (DEP-12); cellular carriers for client gauges
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits under 46 client contracts and manual reading support
single_points_of_failure: Single cloud region for the DSMS ingestion service (standby region holds data only)

business_process: Maintenance management, outage planning, and spare parts
description: Work orders, planned outages, gate and hoist maintenance records, critical spares (SYS-10 enterprise asset management)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Maintenance can run on paper for days; gate testing records (18 CFR 12.54) and Part 12 records must be rebuilt afterward
manual_workaround: Paper work orders; printed spare parts lists
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed outage work and expedited parts
acquired_asset_dependency: PD maintenance records still in the prior owner's system (read-only export)

business_process: Hydro Services field and engineering services
description: Field maintenance and engineering for non-federal dam owners (gates, hoists, trashracks, unit overhauls, inspections)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Revenue of about $2.2 million per working day; crews keep working on site, but billing, scheduling, and engineering files are delayed
manual_workaround: Paper timesheets; crew schedules by phone; engineering files from local copies
quantified_impact_basis: About 20% of daily field services revenue deferred

description: FERC Part 12 reports, Security Program filings, NERC CIP evidence and EOP-004 reports, CIP-008 notifications
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Regulatory clocks keep running in an outage: CIP-008-6 R4 (1 hour after determination), EOP-004-4 (24 hours or next business day), 18 CFR 12.10 (preferably within 72 hours)
manual_workaround: Telephone and email from out-of-band devices; printed contact lists and forms in incident binders
dependent_people_or_facilities: NERC compliance team; dam safety engineers
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time; penalty exposure is the real impact
acquired_asset_dependency: PD reporting contacts not yet in the fleet binders

description: Email, chat, files, phones for 12,000 staff
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Coordination across 46 developments and 14 offices; incident communications move to out-of-band tools
manual_workaround: Out-of-band conferencing and company mobile phones; printed contacts
quantified_impact_basis: Productivity loss across corporate and services staff

description: Monthly close, quarterly and annual filings, SOX controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines; the MTD drops to 48 hours in the quarter-end window
manual_workaround: Manual journal entries; extended close calendar
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and advisor costs; risk of a late filing

description: Payroll for 12,000 employees including seasonal and field staff
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Wage payment laws and union agreements at 11 plants; repeat-prior-payroll fallback works for one cycle
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll; manual adjustments afterward

description: License-required recreation: 26 campgrounds, 140 boat ramps and day-use areas
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Small revenue; FERC expects recreation access to stay open, so walk-in operation continues
